aria: Animated recap of the Grizzlies' 114 to 109 win at Minnesota: Cedric Coward's three with 6:34 left that made it 99 to 87, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Coward's 22 points, the top scorers, how the Grizzlies won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from Hoops Nightly's game page for the Grizzlies' 114–109 win at Minnesota on Nov 27, 2026: all 114 Memphis points and all 109 Minnesota points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (44 of 93, 13 of 35 from three, 13 of 17 FT for Memphis; 42 of 75, 11 of 24, 14 of 23 for Minnesota), assists (19–27), steals (12–8) and bench points (53–23). The quarter scores (32–29–21–32 to 25–25–31–28) match the FOX Sports box score; 61–50 at the half and 82–81 after three are also in WJOX. Points off turnovers (27–19) are on Hoops Nightly and WJOX; second-chance points (25–11), points in the paint (54–60) and the biggest leads (14 and 4) are from Hoops Nightly. Team rebound totals are left out because Hoops Nightly's totals don't match its own player lines. Cedric Coward's assist count differs between Hoops Nightly and Basketball-Reference, so it isn't shown. Records are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Memphis led by 14 late in the second quarter (59–45, FOX play-by-play). Minnesota opened the third on a 26–11 run to lead 76–72 (AP) and led 81–78 late in the quarter; Coward's driving floater with 16 seconds left and his steal and layup with 14 seconds left put Memphis up 82–81, and Minnesota never tied or led again (FOX play-by-play). The Grizzlies started the fourth on a 17–6 run to lead 99–87 (WJOX; FOX play-by-play). Minnesota got within 109–105 on a 10–0 run in the last 2:36 (Hoops Nightly; FOX), but Ty Jerome and Jaylen Wells made 5 of 6 free throws down the stretch (WJOX). Javon Small's 19 tied his season high (AP). Memphis has won 8 of its last 9 (AP) and won NBA Cup West Group B (AP). Minnesota played without Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball (AP; WJOX). Memphis hosts the Lakers on Sunday (AP; Hoops Nightly).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cedric Coward's three with 6:34 left, assisted by Jaylen Wells, that made it 99–87: the FOX Sports play-by-play has it at 6:34 for 96–87 to 99–87, Hoops Nightly lists it as the end of an 8–0 burst, and WJOX and the AP describe Coward's three finishing the run to 99–87. So the board's Grizzlies +9 to +12 is 96–87 to 99–87. The play-by-play calls it a running jump shot; the distance and defender aren't recorded, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Memphis Grizzlies or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Cedric Coward's listed 6-foot-5 and 206 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia, RealGM), with arms scaled to the 7-foot-2¼ wingspan measured at the 2025 draft combine (as reported by SI), in the Grizzlies' road kit with No. 23 (Wikipedia, RealGM). He has no approved look yet, so he is drawn with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
